newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Paranagua port workers to meet operators over pay.
newsitem.headline: Paranagua port workers to meet operators over pay.

text.p: Dockworkers at the centre of a wage dispute at the key Brazilian port of Paranagua were due to meet with port operators on Tuesday to try to avert a threatened strike on Wednesday.

"We are trying to minimise the situation," said the director of the dockworkers' union. "We passed on our position saying that we will cancel the strike if the pay rise is effective as of now and we are awaiting their response."

The dockworkers are asking for a 21 percent pay increase which they say they are owed since last year. Other Paranagua portworkers have threatened to go on strike on Wednesday to support their demand.
Dockworkers are due to meet with the port operators' union SINDOP at around 1000 a.m. local (1300 GMT).
The strike could become nationwide if workers at other ports decide to strike in sympathy on Thursday if no deal is struck.
The dockworkers initially wanted the wage rise to be retroactive but now say they will call off the strike if the pay increase is granted effective from March 1.
